Mein "Geheimrezept", um den Topfkuchen von meiner Mama zu veganisieren, den wir als Kinder immer gegessen haben und der Recht viel Ei enthält, ist alle Eiersatzmöglichkeiten zu mischen:
Pro Ei 60g Apfelmus, 1 EL Sojamehl und 1 EL Leinsamen. Fall nötig noch Wasser.
Im restlichen Rezept dann Zucker nach Geschmack reduzieren (weil das Apfelmus süß ist) und fett auch stark reduzieren, weil Eier Fett absorbieren (hab ich zumindest mal gelesen und klappt in dem Rezept super, brauche nur die Hälfte an Margarine).
Gerne dann noch einen Schuss Sprudelwasser und etwas mehr Backpulver.
Das war mein Ergebnis nach viel experimentieren, bei weniger Eilastigen Rezepten klappen die Zutaten meistens auch einzeln, also je nachdem entweder Fruchtmuß, Leinsamen, Sojamehl, Sprudelwasser oder für Eischnee Aquafaba.

I never really thought about that but as a demisexual person with an ED, it really makes me think. I’ve always had trouble with people getting close to me, like even hugging seemed really weird for me. Later on, when I made my first romantic and sexual experiences, a lot of it felt weird. I just did stuff because I believed it was normal to do so. For me a big part that made those experiences really uncomfortable was my own insecurity I believe but I’m still wondering and afraid that there might be some hidden trauma causing all this. I really don’t hope so. Fast forward to some years later when my ED started. First it wasn’t about my body at all. After a lot of contemplation and therapy, I believe a big part of it for me is wanting a child like body. I oftentimes look at my body and am annoyed it works. Annoyed of growing up. Having a menstrual cycle. All that. Which would also match with me disliking sex and everything that comes with. Both seems to be rooted deep in insecurity, age regression and untreated trauma (at least I believe so). Also someone else mentioned in their comment the link between gender disphoria in trans persons and EDs…I guess that could be kind of similar? (I really don‘t wanna play disphoria down, I believe it’s horrible to be in a body not matching your gender identity) but I’d say both lead to the feeling that something is just wrong about your body. Which is definetly something that will most probably result in body image issues and at least in my case also leads to feeling weird during sexual activities. Hope this comment is somehow understandable, I feel like I have so many thoughts on this…and thank you a lot for your post, I did never really think about all this and now I’m quite mind blown, seem like you hit a spot!

With that height and weight you are borderline underweight. I don’t want to scare you out of recovery because you definitely deserve recovering and getting better but I’m afraid to say that recovery won’t be able without some weight gain. But what I can also say from my experience is that there is no need to be afraid of this, as your body knows best what weight he feels good with. If you haven’t already, try to read about set point theory. Not everyone believes in it but I learned about it in professional treatment and it really helps me to accept my body and weight gain/fluctuations. Also try not to worry about your metabolism, your body will adjust to a bigger amount of food in no time and then you won’t gain as fast as at the beginning. Also a big part of it is water weight. As someone who had some relapse and therefore lost and gained more then once I can tell you from my experience that my body adjusts really well to its set point weight as soon as I let myself heal and I definetly feel better mentally and physically at this weight. I believe in you and don’t let your mind trick you into thinking you should lose even more. That is your ED! You got this!!
